title: UI config copy goes stale: patchConfig sends the whole stale config and ignores the core's corrected reply
claim: patchConfig in src/store.ts:362-373 does `const config = { ...get().config, ...patch }; set({ config }); ... await api.setConfig(config);`, and src/lib/ipc.ts:47 types it as `setConfig: (config: AppConfig) => invoke<void>("set_config", { config })` (also listed under the report's IPC-contract-drift finding: setConfig is typed void but the command returns a config). The core command actually returns AppConfig (commands.rs:55-59) after rewriting it: while a recording runs, a source change is reverted and the core calls `crate::notify(&app, "error", "Stop the recording before changing the source.")` (commands.rs:72-81); the encoder is replaced by `encode::resolve(...)` (state.rs:367); accent colours are cleaned. The UI discards that reply and keeps (and later resends) its own uncorrected whole config. The core also edits the config on its own and never tells the UI: `repair_screens()` (lib.rs:472-507, called on monitor changes at lib.rs:542 and :586) rewrites `recording.target_id`, the overlay screen and the console screen; there is no `config-changed` event.
scenario: (a) During a recording the user picks another monitor; the core refuses but the tile stays "Selected". Every later unrelated toggle (a sound, the watermark) resends that target and shows the error toast again; once the recording stops, the next unrelated toggle silently applies the change and restarts the buffer (commands.rs:110-118), discarding buffered footage. (b) The user plugs/unplugs a monitor and `\\.\DISPLAYn` is renumbered; the next unrelated setting change sends the old `targetId`, `target_changed` is true, the replay buffer restarts and everything it held is lost. (c) The user selects an encoder marked "(not available)" (selectable, Recording.tsx:353-356); UI and Dashboard keep showing it while the core runs a fallback.
fix: 1) Type `set_config` as `invoke<AppConfig>` and apply the reply behind a version guard (same ticket pattern as `clips-changed` at store.ts:301): `const v = ++cfgVersion; const next = await api.setConfig(config); if (v === cfgVersion) set({ config: next });`. 2) Emit `config-changed` from the core after `repair_screens`, the tray hint and token changes, and listen for it in `init`. 3) Better: replace the whole-config write with a core-side merged `patch_config(patch)`.

No `config-changed` emitter exists (grep of src-tauri/src for emit with config: none); the UI reads config only once at init (store.ts:263). Recording.tsx:242-248 tile click has no is-recording guard; Recording.tsx:352-356 unavailable encoders remain selectable. capture.rs:418-425 pick resolves by stable id first, so the restarted buffer in (b) lands on the right screen; the loss is the spurious restart itself. votes.reachable_by: Any local user through normal UI use: (a) picking another monitor tile during a manual recording, then toggling any other setting; (b) a monitor hot-plug/dock/driver reset that renumbers \\.\DISPLAYn while the app is open (needs a stable panel id, which repair requires), followed by any settings change while the replay buffer runs; (c) choosing an encoder marked '(not available)'. No remote or untrusted input involved.
votes.fix_assessment: Fix 1 (type set_config as AppConfig and apply the reply behind a version ticket) is correct and fixes (a) and (c); fix 2 is needed for (b), but the tray-hint and token parts are already guarded in the core (commands.rs:66, :82). A smaller core-only fix for the buffer loss in (b): in set_config, when the incoming target_stable_id equals previous.target_stable_id (and is Some), keep previous.target_id before computing target_changed (or run capture::repair on the incoming recording/overlay/console choice only when the device name differs). That way a stale page cannot trigger a restart, without running a monitor enumeration on every slider move. Fix 3 (core-side merged patch_config) is the robust long-term option.

UI loads config only once at init (store.ts:263); grep finds no config-changed listener. votes.corrected_claim: Accurate in mechanism and location. Two minor corrections: (1) the delayed source change after the recording stops is not fully silent - start_buffer_and_notify (lib.rs:345-361) shows a 'Replay buffer running' toast/banner and plays a sound - but it happens on an unrelated toggle and still discards the buffered footage; (2) the staleness is partly self-healing: setHotkeys, setClipDir, regenerateControlToken, upsertSource and removeSource (store.ts:392-429) replace the UI copy with the core's reply, so any of those actions resyncs it. Additional consequence not in the claim: after a runtime renumber (scenario b) while a recording runs, every unrelated toggle also triggers the 'Stop the recording before changing the source.' error toast.
votes.reachable_by: The user in ordinary use, from the main window. (a) Pick a different monitor/window tile on the Video page while a recording runs, then change any other setting that goes through patchConfig (Behaviour, Banner, Console, Friends, sounds, etc.). (b) No mistake needed: a monitor hot-plug, a dock, or a display waking from sleep that makes Windows hand out a new \\.\DISPLAYn while ClippiBoy runs; watch_monitors repairs the core copy every tick, and the next settings change from the UI restarts the buffer. (c) Choose an encoder labelled '(not available)'. Likelihood: (b) and (c) are fairly common on multi-monitor setups and with hardware encoders missing; (a) is rarer. The loss is the in-memory replay buffer (minutes of footage), not saved clips.
votes.fix_assessment: Part 1 (type the reply as AppConfig and apply it behind a monotonic ticket, like clips-changed at store.ts:301) fixes (a) and (c) and is cheap. On its own it does not fix (b), because the core's repair_screens never reaches the UI. That needs part 2 (emit config-changed after repair_screens and listen in init) or part 3 (a core-side merged patch_config), and part 3 also removes the whole-config-resend class of bugs.

title: Hotkey recorder cannot be started from the keyboard; recorder/Unbind buttons not tied to row labels
claim: In settings/Hotkeys.tsx:329-333 recording starts only on `onMouseDown`; Enter/Space fire `click`, not mousedown, so keyboard users cannot assign hotkeys. The recorder button and the "Unbind" buttons are not associated with their row labels.
scenario: A keyboard-only user tabs to a hotkey recorder and presses Enter or Space; nothing starts recording, so they cannot assign hotkeys. Screen readers announce the buttons without the row's label.
fix: Add an `onClick`/`onKeyDown` path to start recording, and tie the recorder and Unbind buttons to their row labels.

votes.evidence: src/routes/settings/Hotkeys.tsx:326-333 the recorder
votes.reachable_by: Any keyboard-only or screen-reader user on Settings > Hotkeys (all five rows: Save clip, Buffer on/off, Screenshot, Recording, Console). Mouse users are unaffected.
votes.fix_assessment: Do not simply add onClick next to the existing onMouseDown toggle: a mouse click would fire both and toggle twice. Move the toggle to onClick, keep onMouseDown only for stopPropagation (so the window mousedown listener at Hotkeys.tsx:310 does not end recording), and give the recorder and Unbind buttons names that include the row label (e.g. aria-label=`Unbind ${label}` / aria-labelledby the Row label id).

votes.evidence: src/routes/settings/Hotkeys.tsx:326-333: `
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use by a keyboard-only or screen-reader user in Settings > Hotkeys. Not a security issue. Defaults exist (config.rs:47 `save_clip_hotkey: "Ctrl+Shift+S"`, model.rs:384 `Alt+C`), so such a user keeps the default bindings and can still unbind via the × button (which has onClick), but cannot assign or change any of the five hotkeys.

title: Mixer M/S/⧉ buttons and label input are unnamed and lack state

title: Gallery tile actions stay invisible when keyboard-focused
claim: The heart, folder and delete buttons on tiles use `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` (Clips.tsx:560, :572) with no `focus-visible`/`group-focus-within` reveal.
scenario: A keyboard user tabs through the gallery and focus lands on invisible buttons.
fix: Reveal the actions on `focus-visible` / `group-focus-within`.

Tile wrapper Card has `"group overflow-hidden"` (Clips.tsx:436) and no focus-within variant; grep finds no `group-focus`/`focus-within` anywhere in src. The global ring `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent) }` (index.css:64) is painted on an element whose own opacity (heart) or ancestor opacity (folder/delete) is 0, so the ring is invisible too. Contrast: Friends.tsx:441/450 and Clips.tsx:1109 already use `focus-visible:opacity-100` for the same pattern.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use: any user pressing Tab in the Clips gallery. After the thumbnail button, focus moves onto the heart (when the clip is not yet a favorite), then Show in folder and Delete clip, all invisible, and the focus ring is hidden as well. A mouse-first game-clip app has few keyboard-only users, so real-world impact is small.
votes.fix_assessment: The fix is correct and cheap. Add `focus-visible:opacity-100` to the heart button and `group-focus-within:opacity-100` (or `focus-within:opacity-100`) to the action wrapper div, matching what Friends.tsx already does.

scenario: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot open recent clips or stat targets from the Dashboard.

title: Menu opened by keyboard on Friends "More" appears top-left
claim: A menu opened by keyboard-activating "More" (Friends.tsx:448, `onClick={openMenu}`) is positioned from the event's `clientX/Y`, which are 0 for keyboard-generated clicks.
scenario: A keyboard user presses Enter on "More" and the menu appears at the top-left corner of the window, away from the button.
fix: Use the button's bounding rect when `event.detail === 0`.

votes.evidence: src/routes/Friends.tsx:446-449 `<button aria-label={`More for ${friend.displayName}`} onClick={openMenu} ... focus-visible:opacity-100>` is a normal tabbable button. openMenu (Friends.tsx:368-369) passes the click event straight to `menu.open(event, [...])`, and src/components/ui/Menu.tsx:84-86 stores `x: trigger.clientX, y: trigger.clientY` without looking at the trigger element. A click that Chromium/WebView2 synthesises from Enter/Space on a button is positionless (clientX = clientY = 0, detail = 0). Surface's layout effect (Menu.tsx:124-128) then clamps it to `Math.max(EDGE, ...)` = (8, 8), the top-left of the window. Neither file checks event.detail or calls getBoundingClientRect on the trigger.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary local use: a keyboard user who Tabs to a friend row's 'More' button on the Friends page and presses Enter or Space. The menu still works from the keyboard (Arrow keys and Enter through the window capture listener at Menu.tsx:156-182). It just opens about 8 px from the window's top-left corner, away from the row. The context-menu key and Shift+F10 open it through the row's onContextMenu, which Chromium places at the focused element, so those are unaffected.
votes.fix_assessment: The proposed fix is correct and small: in openMenu, when event.detail === 0, call menu.open with clientX/clientY taken from event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect() (for example left/bottom), plus the event's preventDefault and stopPropagation.

votes.evidence: src/routes/Friends.tsx:448 `<button aria-label={`More for ${friend.displayName}`} onClick={openMenu} ... focus-visible:opacity-100>` (a reachable tab stop). Friends.tsx:368 `const openMenu = (event: MouseEvent) => menu.open(event, [...])` passes the click event straight through. src/components/ui/Menu.tsx:84-86 `setOpen({ x: trigger.clientX, y: trigger.clientY, ... })` has no fallback to an element rect. Menu.tsx:121-128 only clamps: `x: Math.max(EDGE, Math.min(x, ...))` with EDGE = 8 (line 105). Menu.tsx:202 `style={{ left: at.x, top: at.y }}` on a `fixed` surface. No code in src checks event.detail or uses a trigger rect for menus (grep finds none). A keyboard-activated button click is a synthetic, positionless click (clientX/clientY = 0, detail = 0) under the HTML 'fire a synthetic pointer event' rules and in Chromium/WebView2. That leads to (0,0), clamped to (8,8): the top-left of the window.
votes.reachable_by: A keyboard user who tabs to a friend row's 'More' button and presses Enter or Space. The menu still works with arrow keys and Enter (Menu.tsx:156-176), but it shows up far away from the button.
votes.fix_assessment: Using event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect() (for example its bottom-left) when event.detail === 0 fixes it. Put the fix in the button's own onClick handler, not in the shared openMenu, because the row's onContextMenu (Friends.tsx:410) also calls openMenu with a real pointer position. A better place would be a helper in Menu.tsx, so that clipMenu and other button-opened menus get the same fallback.

title: Menu lacks Home/End/Tab handling and aria-activedescendant
claim: The Menu component has no Home/End/Tab keyboard handling and no `aria-activedescendant`.
scenario: Keyboard users cannot jump to first/last items or Tab out cleanly, and screen readers are not told which item is active.
fix: Add Home/End/Tab handling and `aria-activedescendant`.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/Menu.tsx:156-176 onKey handles only "Escape", "ArrowDown"/"ArrowUp" and `event.key === "Enter" && active >= 0`; no Home/End/Tab branch, so Tab moves focus in the page underneath while the menu stays open (no focusin/focusout listener; it closes only on pointerdown outside, blur, resize, scroll at :179-184). Menu.tsx:195-200 `role="menu"` with no aria-activedescendant, and the comment at :198-200 says "The menu deliberately takes no focus" (onMouseDown preventDefault). Active item is shown only by a CSS class at :227. Mitigations: ArrowUp from nothing selects the last item and arrows wrap (:168-169), so first/last are one keypress away. Reachability: the menu opens on contextmenu events (TextMenu.tsx:117/120 document listener, Clips.tsx:442, Friends.tsx:410, clipMenu.tsx:246, ClipPlayer/ShotViewer), which the keyboard ContextMenu key / Shift+F10 also fires on the focused element, so keyboard users can open it.
votes.corrected_claim: The facts hold, but the screen-reader gap is wider than stated: focus never moves into the menu (Menu.tsx:198-200), so assistive tech is not told the menu opened at all, not just which item is active. Missing Home/End costs little because the arrows wrap. The worse Tab problem is that the menu stays open while focus moves on.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use by keyboard-only or screen-reader users of the desktop app (right-click menus on clips, friends and text fields, opened with the ContextMenu key or Shift+F10). It has no security impact and is of limited practical reach in a mouse-centric game-capture app.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding Home/End is trivial, and Tab should close the menu. But aria-activedescendant on the role=menu div would be ignored, because only the element that holds DOM focus can carry it. That needs either moving focus into the menu (against the deliberate design that keeps text-field selection and avoids an editor blur-save) or setting aria-activedescendant/aria-owns on the still-focused trigger element.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/Menu.tsx:156-176: the window keydown handler handles only `Escape`, `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` (which wrap: `selectable[(next + selectable.length) % selectable.length]`, :169) and `Enter` (`if (event.key === "Enter" && active >= 0)`, :173). It has no Home, End, Tab or Space branch, and there is no `aria-activedescendant` anywhere in src. Menu.tsx:198-199 is decisive for the screen-reader part: `// The menu deliberately takes no focus: the text field underneath would otherwise lose its selection`. Focus stays on the trigger or text field, and `active` (:117) only switches a background class (:227). Tab is not swallowed and does not close the menu (closing happens only on pointerdown outside, blur, resize, scroll or Escape, :179-184). So Tab moves focus through the page underneath while the menu stays open, and because the buttons sit at the end of the portal host (:99) Tab can also land on them.
votes.corrected_claim: Literally true, but the details are off. (1) Home/End: arrow navigation wraps, and the first ArrowDown/ArrowUp jumps straight to the first/last item (:168). Under the WAI-ARIA APG, Home/End are required only when wrapping is not supported, so this part is a minor gap. (2) The real Tab problem is that Tab neither closes the menu nor is trapped. Focus moves on underneath while a stale menu stays open, and keyboard Enter keeps firing the highlighted item (:173) wherever focus has gone. (3) Screen readers learn nothing because focus never enters the menu, by design (:198-199). Adding `aria-activedescendant` to the role=menu div would do nothing, because that attribute only works on the element that holds DOM focus. Impact is an a11y gap, not a functional break: the menu is a context-menu convenience, and its actions (clip actions, text-field cut/copy/paste) have other routes.
votes.reachable_by: Keyboard and screen-reader users who open a context menu (the Menu key or Shift+F10 fires `contextmenu`, which TextMenu.tsx:57-120, Clips.tsx:442, Friends.tsx:410 and clipMenu.tsx:246 turn into `menu.open`).
votes.fix_assessment: Home/End are a cheap win, and the most useful change is to close the menu on Tab. Putting `aria-activedescendant` on the menu container will not work while the menu takes no focus. It would have to sit on the focused element (for example the text field, pointing at item ids), or the menu would have to take focus and restore the selection afterwards.

title: Missing ARIA state on Segmented, NavBar and Toasts
claim: `Segmented` has no `aria-pressed` or radiogroup semantics; the NavBar has no `aria-current="page"`; Toasts have no live region.
scenario: Screen-reader users cannot tell which segment or page is selected, and toast messages are never announced.
fix: Add radiogroup/`aria-pressed` semantics to Segmented, `aria-current="page"` to the active NavBar item and an `aria-live` region for Toasts.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/Controls.tsx:62-86: Segmented renders a plain `<div className=...>` with no role and buttons that have only `key`, `data-slide`, `onClick` and `className`. Selection is shown only by `value === key ? "text-black" : "text-ink-muted ..."` (:81) and the sliding pill. There is no aria-pressed, aria-checked or radiogroup. src/components/NavBar.tsx:57-67: nav buttons carry `onClick` and `className` (`route === id ? "text-ink" : "text-ink-muted ..."`) and no aria-current. src/components/Toasts.tsx:81-99: the toast stack is `<div ref={stack} className="pointer-events-none fixed ...">` with no role and no aria-live, and the messages are added dynamically through the `notice` event (:44-46). A grep of src finds no aria-live anywhere. The only role="status" is src/console/Trouble.tsx:129, which belongs to a different window. App.tsx:92 mounts `<Toasts />` with no wrapping live region. Toggle (:17-19) does use role=switch and aria-checked, which shows the omission in Segmented is not deliberate.
votes.reachable_by: Screen-reader users on any Segmented control (settings index, Colors, Banner, Console, Friends, Setup, ShotViewer), on the NavBar, and for every `notice` event emitted by the backend (including error toasts, which show for 6 s and are never announced).
votes.fix_assessment: The fix is right and cheap. Use role=radiogroup/radio with aria-checked (or aria-pressed) on Segmented, aria-current="page" on the active NavBar button, and role="status"/aria-live="polite" on the toast stack (role="alert" for errors). A related bug to fix at the same time: Segmented's `disabled` only adds `pointer-events-none` on the wrapper (:65) and never sets `disabled` or aria-disabled on the buttons. In Banner.tsx:148 and Console.tsx:118 keyboard users can therefore still Tab to and activate a 'disabled' segment.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/Controls.tsx:62-86 Segmented renders a plain <div> with <button onClick={() => onChange(key)}> per option; selection is only `value === key ? "text-black" : "text-ink-muted ..."` (:81) plus an aria-hidden SlidingIndicator (SlidingIndicator.tsx:72-74); no role=radiogroup/radio, aria-checked or aria-pressed. Also, `disabled` only adds `pointer-events-none opacity-40` to the wrapper (:65) and never sets disabled on the buttons, so keyboard users can still Tab to and activate a 'disabled' Segmented. src/components/NavBar.tsx:57-66 nav buttons have no aria-current; active state is only `route === id ? "text-ink" : ...`. src/components/Toasts.tsx:81-84 the container has no aria-live/role=status/alert, and grep finds no live region anywhere in src/ except console/Trouble.tsx:129. Reachable: App.tsx:64 and :92 render NavBar and Toasts always, Segmented is used in 9 places (settings, Setup, ShotViewer), and toasts come from lib.rs:57-64 notify() on clip saves and errors.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate. One addition: Segmented's `disabled` prop does not disable its buttons for keyboard users (Controls.tsx:65), so a keyboard user can still change a 'disabled' setting.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use by screen-reader users on every page (the nav bar and toasts are always mounted) and in every settings page that uses Segmented. It has no security impact.
votes.fix_assessment: The proposed fix is correct and cheap. The toast container is already always mounted (Toasts.tsx:77-79), so adding role=status/aria-live=polite to it (aria-live=assertive or role=alert for error toasts) will announce reliably. aria-pressed or role=radio+aria-checked on Segmented buttons and aria-current="page" on the active NavBar button are one-liners. Segmented should also pass `disabled` through to its buttons.

title: --color-ink-faint fails WCAG AA contrast
claim: `--color-ink-faint: #5c5c68` measures 2.84:1 on surface, 2.63:1 on elevated and 3.04:1 on base, failing WCAG AA; it is used 83 times, mostly for small hint text.
scenario: Low-vision users cannot read hint text rendered in ink-faint.
fix: Use `#80808c`, which gives 4.79:1 and 4.44:1.

votes.evidence:
src/styles/tokens.css:4-7,14: `--color-base: #08080a; --color-surface: #121215; --color-elevated: #1a1a1f; --color-hover: #22222a; ... --color-ink-faint: #5c5c68;`. Computed WCAG relative-luminance ratios: #5c5c68 on base 3.04, surface 2.84, elevated 2.63, hover 2.39. No runtime override of the token exists (only definition is tokens.css:14; lib/accent.ts does not touch ink colors). grep finds 88 'ink-faint' occurrences in src/, 83 of them text-ink-faint/placeholder:text-ink-faint, almost all on text-xs/text-[11px]/text-[10px] hint lines (e.g. routes/settings/Storage.tsx:108 `

{hint}

`, Dashboard.tsx:316, Console.tsx:1525), plus inactive nav labels (NavBar.tsx:164) and placeholders. Small text needs 4.5:1, so every use fails 1.4.3; the bg-ink-faint status dots (Friends.tsx:492, console/Friends.tsx:224) also miss the 3:1 non-text threshold on surface.
votes.reachable_by: Any user viewing settings hints, empty states, placeholders, inactive nav items and metadata labels; worst for low-vision users and on bg-elevated/bg-hover cards.
votes.fix_assessment: Lightening the token is the right single-point fix, but the proposed #80808c only reaches 4.44:1 on --color-elevated (and 4.05:1 on --color-hover), so it still fails AA there; something around #868692 or higher is needed, which nearly collapses into --color-ink-muted (#8a8a96), so the faint/muted hierarchy would need rethinking.

votes.evidence: src/styles/tokens.css:4-6,14: `--color-base: #08080a; --color-surface: #121215; --color-elevated: #1a1a1f; ... --color-ink-faint: #5c5c68;`. Recomputed WCAG 2.x ratios: 3.04:1 on base, 2.84:1 on surface, 2.63:1 on elevated, 2.39:1 on hover #22222a, 2.75:1 on the console HUD (--hud-top rgba(23,20,32,.96)), all under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text. The app is dark-only: src/index.css:19-21 sets `body { background: var(--color-base) }`, and nothing in src/lib overrides ink-faint (accent.ts swaps only the accent and logo shades). The token appears 87 times outside its definition (88 counting tokens.css), not 83. Nearly all are small text: `text-xs text-ink-faint` hints (Recording.tsx:220/253/278/447/479, Storage.tsx:108/204/370, Hotkeys.tsx:255, About.tsx:122, ExportDialog.tsx:155/196), `text-[11px]` labels (Setup.tsx:412/425, Console.tsx:819/1048/1122), and placeholders (Clips.tsx:768/789, ClipMeta.tsx:210/308, Friends.tsx:206/259). Some sit on elevated: AudioMixer.tsx:627 `bg-elevated text-ink-faint`. A few are non-text (status dots at Friends.tsx:492, settings/shared.tsx:114; icons at Clips.tsx:782/796, Console.tsx:1391), and even those miss the 3:1 non-text minimum on surface and elevated.
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism and the ratios are correct. The token appears 87 times rather than 83. The proposed replacement #80808c is still below AA on the elevated surface (4.44:1) and the hover surface (4.05:1).
votes.reachable_by: Every user in ordinary use: the hint text, placeholders and sub-labels render on almost every screen of the main window and the in-game console. It hurts low-vision users most, and is worse on a dim screen or in the overlay over a bright game. It is purely visual, with no security or data impact.
votes.fix_assessment: #80808c clears 4.5:1 on base and surface but not on elevated (4.44) or hover (4.05). AA on elevated needs at least about #81818d, and on hover about #888894, which is practically ink-muted #8a8a96, itself only 4.63:1 on hover. The real fix is to raise ink-faint to about #83838f or more and accept a smaller gap from ink-muted, or keep faint only for non-text and large text and move the small hints to ink-muted.

title: Reduced-motion rule covers only cb-* animations
claim: The reduced-motion block at motion.css:377 covers only `cb-*` animations; Tailwind `transition-*`, `SlidingIndicator` and `animate-pulse` (Friends.tsx:164) ignore `prefers-reduced-motion`.
scenario: A user with reduced motion enabled still sees transitions, the sliding indicator and pulsing placeholders.
fix: Add `motion-reduce:transition-none` or a global reduced-motion rule.

votes.evidence: src/styles/motion.css:377-383: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { [class*="cb-"] { animation-duration: 1ms !important; animation-delay: 0ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; } }` - only animation properties, only on elements whose class contains 'cb-'; no transition override and no other global reduced-motion rule in src/ (others are scoped: console/console.css:735,1215 and overlay/overlay.css:230,330 only for cb-dock/cb-sheet/cb-card etc.). src/components/ui/SlidingIndicator.tsx:79 `"transition-[transform,width] duration-[260ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-soft)]"` with no prefersReducedMotion() check (used by NavBar.tsx:54 and Controls.tsx:70). src/routes/Friends.tsx:164 `<Card className="h-[112px] animate-pulse" />`, and Card.tsx:12 classes contain no 'cb-', so the infinite pulse is not matched. Tailwind transform transitions likewise unguarded: Menu.tsx:207, Button.tsx:37, ColorPicker.tsx:141, Controls.tsx:32. JS-driven animations (lib/motion.ts animate(), useFlip, usePresence, useCountUp) do honour the setting, which the claim does not contradict.
votes.reachable_by: Any user with the OS 'reduce motion / show animations off' setting, on the main window's nav bar, segmented controls, menus, buttons and the Friends profile loading placeholder.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding motion-reduce:transition-none to SlidingIndicator, Menu and similar, swapping animate-pulse for motion-safe:animate-pulse, or adding a global `*{transition-duration:1ms!important}` under the media query would fix it. The remaining motion is short and mostly colour/opacity (pulse is opacity only), and prefers-reduced-motion maps to WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA), so this is low severity rather than medium.

votes.evidence: src/styles/motion.css:377-383: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { [class*="cb-"] { animation-duration: 1ms !important; animation-delay: 0ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; } }`. It touches only CSS animations on elements whose class contains `cb-`, never `transition-*`, not even cb- transitions such as `.cb-ring-arc { transition: stroke-dashoffset 600ms linear }` at motion.css:353. Grepping src for `motion-reduce` or `motion-safe` finds nothing. src/components/ui/SlidingIndicator.tsx: `"transition-[transform,width] duration-[260ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-soft)]"`, with JS setting `pill.style.transform = translate(...)` and no prefersReducedMotion() check. It is used by NavBar.tsx:54 (every route change) and Controls.tsx:70 (segmented controls). src/routes/Friends.tsx:164: `if (!me) return <Card className="h-[112px] animate-pulse" />;`. Card.tsx:12 adds no cb- class, so Tailwind's infinite pulse is not caught by the selector. The JS side is covered: src/lib/motion.ts animate() returns null when reduced motion is on, and useFlip, usePresence, useCountUp, ClipPlayer, ShotViewer and BusyVeil all check prefersReducedMotion(). overlay.css:230/330 and console.css:735/1215 have their own blocks.
votes.corrected_claim: The facts are correct, but the impact is smaller than 'medium' suggests. Of 86 Tailwind transitions in .tsx files, 61 are colour or opacity fades (51 transition-colors, 10 transition-opacity), which are not vestibular motion. About 20 move transform, width or height for 200-300ms: SlidingIndicator, transition-transform, transition-[width] and similar. The pulse is an opacity pulse, shown only while signed in before the friends profile (`me`) arrives. WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) is a AAA criterion.
votes.reachable_by: Any user who turned on the OS 'reduce motion' setting (on Windows, Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Animation effects off, which WebView2 reports as prefers-reduced-motion). They see it in ordinary use: switching routes in the NavBar, changing a segmented control, or opening Friends while signed in before the profile loads. Nothing else can trigger it, and there is no security impact.
votes.fix_assessment: A global rule under the existing media query, for example `*, ::before, ::after { transition-duration: 1ms !important; animation-duration: 1ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; }`, covers it in one place and keeps the 'ends in its final state' contract. Nothing in src listens for transitionend, so it is safe; only Console.tsx:920 uses onAnimationEnd, and 1ms still fires it. Sprinkling `motion-reduce:transition-none` per call site would be easy to miss.

title: No pull-request CI: nothing runs tsc on PRs
claim: `.github/workflows` only contains release, ffmpeg and pages workflows; nothing runs `tsc` (or lint/tests) on pull requests.
scenario: A PR that breaks type-checking or the Rust tests is merged without any automated check.
fix: Add a `ci.yml` on `pull_request` running `npm ci && tsc --noEmit && eslint . && vitest run`, plus `cargo test` on Windows.

votes.evidence: .github/workflows has only ffmpeg.yml (`on: push: tags: ["ffmpeg-*"]`), pages.yml (`push: branches: [main] paths: ["site/**", ...]`, workflow_dispatch, workflow_run) and release.yml (`push: tags: ["v*"]`, workflow_dispatch). None has a `pull_request` trigger and none runs cargo test, `npm test` in server/, or a linter. No local hook substitutes for it: there is no .husky, lefthook or pre-commit config, and .git/hooks holds only samples. One detail the claim leaves out: tsc does run at release time, because release.yml calls tauri-action -> `tauri build` -> src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:9 `"beforeBuildCommand": "npm run build"` -> package.json `"build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build"`. title: Startup snapshots in friends/share stores can overwrite newer pushes
claim: friends.ts:42-43 and share.ts:40-41 register `listen` and fire the initial snapshot `invoke` in parallel; the snapshot reply is applied with `setState(view, true)` regardless of whether a push already arrived.
scenario: A push event arrives before the snapshot reply; the older snapshot then replaces the newer pushed state.
fix: Ignore the snapshot if an event has already arrived, or add a version field.

also.title: Store initialisation races invoke() against listen()
also.claim: share.ts:39-42 and friends.ts initialise with `invoke(...)` racing `listen(...)`, so an older snapshot can overwrite a newer event.
also.fix: Fetch after listening, or keep a version counter.

votes.evidence: src/lib/friends.ts:41-44 `void listen<FriendsView>("friends-state", (event) => useFriends.setState(event.payload, true)); void invoke<FriendsView>("friends_state").then((view) => useFriends.setState(view, true));` and src/lib/share.ts:39-42 same pattern for share-state/share_state; neither has a flag/version. Core side: src-tauri/src/friends.rs:188-190 `friends.view.lock().clone()` (snapshot), friends.rs:800-803 `emit` clones the view and `app.emit("friends-state", view)`; share.rs:235-237 / share.rs:1059-1061 likewise. Tauri 2.11.5 delivers events via `webview.eval` (tauri-2.11.5/src/webview/mod.rs:1974-1975 emit_js -> eval) while the command reply travels back on the IPC protocol response (src/ipc/protocol.rs respond), two independent channels with no ordering guarantee. node_modules/@tauri-apps/api/event.js:71-82 shows listen() sends its IPC synchronously before the snapshot invoke is issued, so a push emitted after the core reads the snapshot can land in JS before the snapshot reply, and `setState(view, true)` then replaces it.
votes.corrected_claim: Real but narrow: the window is only between the core cloning the state for the snapshot and the reply reaching JS. It is reachable at startup for friends (main and console windows are both created at startup, console.rs:54-56, while friends.rs is signing in/connecting and emitting), and the stale view persists until the next friends-state/share-state push. For share.rs the transfer list is in-memory and empty at startup, so the share variant is practically unreachable. The "also" fix (FP-55: fetch after awaiting listen) would not fix this overwrite; it only addresses missed events.
votes.reachable_by: Core state pushes (friends sign-in/connection/presence, transfer progress) emitted in the few-millisecond window while the main or console window's module-level snapshot invoke is in flight at page load.
votes.fix_assessment: Setting a `pushed` flag in the listener and skipping the snapshot's setState when it is set works, because the listen IPC is issued before the snapshot invoke; a monotonically increasing version field from the core is more robust. Awaiting listen before invoke alone does not close this race.

title: init() is not idempotent; listeners register twice and are never removed
claim: App.tsx:31-33 calls `void init()` in an effect, which StrictMode runs twice in dev. Every `listen()` in store.ts:272-332 registers twice and is never removed. In browser mode there are two 80 ms intervals (store.ts:228). Vite HMR repeats this for the module-level listeners in friends.ts, share.ts, links.ts and hidden.ts.
scenario: In dev, events are handled twice and `clips-changed` triggers two reads; HMR accumulates duplicate listeners. (Dev only.)
fix: A module-level `initPromise ??= ...` guard, and keep the unlisten handles.

votes.evidence: src/main.tsx:12 `<React.StrictMode>` wraps App; src/App.tsx:32-34 `useEffect(() => { void init(); }, [init]);` with no cleanup and no guard; src/store.ts:216-340 init() has no once-guard, every `await events.onX(...)` return value (UnlistenFn, ipc.ts:205-219 `listen(...)`) is discarded; store.ts:228 `setInterval(..., 80)` in browser mode with no handle kept; store.ts:301-310 `let reads = 0` is local to each init() call, so each of the two clips-changed handlers runs its own listClips() and both apply. friends.ts:41-44, share.ts:39-42, links.ts:123-144 (3 listen + 2 setInterval) and hidden.ts:11-22 (listen + window focus listener) register at module top level with no import.meta.hot dispose (grep finds no `import.meta.hot` in src). init() is called only from App.tsx:33.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate, dev-only. Nuance for HMR: a re-executed friends/share/links module creates a new zustand store, so the leaked old listeners write into the orphaned old store rather than handling events twice on the live one; it is a growing handler/interval leak (and links.ts's old intervals keep calling refresh on the dead store). Under StrictMode the duplicate handlers on the live store are mostly idempotent (clip-saved dedupes by id, others are plain set()); the visible cost is doubled IPC (two listClips per clips-changed, two Promise.all startup reads).
votes.reachable_by: Developers only: React StrictMode double-invoking effects in `tauri dev`/vite dev, and Vite HMR edits to the listed modules. Production builds call the effect once.
votes.fix_assessment: A module-level `initPromise ??= (async () => ...)()` guard in init() fixes the StrictMode duplication; for HMR the module-level listeners would additionally need `import.meta.hot?.dispose` to call the kept unlisten handles and clear the intervals.

claim: The effect in Menu.tsx:143-192 depends on `selectable` and `run`, which are new on every render, so it removes and re-adds five window listeners on every render.

title: SlidingIndicator transitions width
claim: `SlidingIndicator` transitions `width` (a layout property) rather than a transform.
scenario: Each indicator move triggers layout on every animation frame.
fix: Animate with `transform` (scaleX/translateX) instead of width.

title: Main window keeps rendering and receiving 20 Hz IPC while the user is gaming
claim: tauri.conf.json:27 gives the main window `--disable-features=...CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding`; per overlay.rs:40-56 and the README these flags exist for the banner, which now has its own data dir and browser process. The core emits `audio-levels` to `main` at 20 Hz whenever the window is visible and not minimized (lib.rs:964-967), including when behind the game, and store.ts:272 does `set({ levels })` on every page even with no meter on screen; each `set` runs every subscriber's selector (the gallery has one per tile, `NameField`, Clips.tsx:707). NavBar.tsx:176 renders `<LiveDot />` whenever the buffer runs, an infinite animation (motion.css:132-134, `cb-live-ring 2s infinite`) inside a `backdropFilter: "blur(20px)"` pill (NavBar.tsx:49), so the compositor produces frames continuously and likely re-blurs each frame. In RGB accent mode accent.ts:157 runs `setInterval(refresh, 80)` rewriting 16 root custom properties (whole-document style recalc), gated only by `!document.hidden`, which does not change when the window is merely occluded once occlusion detection is off.
scenario: While the user is gaming with ClippiBoy's main window open behind the game, the main window keeps animating, re-blurring, recalculating styles every 80 ms in RGB mode (huge with a 1000-tile gallery) and processing 20 Hz level IPC that notifies every store subscriber, costing CPU/GPU during gameplay. The per-tile NameField selector is a trivial stable-function lookup that never re-renders, so the 20 Hz IPC adds only an event parse and a few thousand no-op selector calls per second. When it runs, each set() only re-runs trivial selectors such as `state.updateClip`, which return stable values, so nothing re-renders; 1000 tiles at 20 Hz is about 20k no-op calls per second. title: Focus is lost to <body> when delete is swapped for ConfirmDelete

scenario: A keyboard user activates delete and loses their place; the next Tab starts from the top of the document.
fix: Move focus to ConfirmDelete's Cancel button (the safe default).

votes.evidence: Every caller swaps the focused trigger for the question by conditional render, e.g. src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:963-979 `{askingDelete ? (<ConfirmDelete ... onCancel={() => setAskingDelete(false)} />) : (<Button ... onClick={() => setAskingDelete(true)}>Delete</Button>)}`; the same pattern is at ShotViewer.tsx:1078/1216, ClipEditor.tsx:186, settings/Friends.tsx:141, Clips.tsx:575/586 and Console.tsx:693. ConfirmDelete.tsx:11-13 deliberately takes no focus ("unlike that one it does **not** focus its own confirm button"), and there is no autoFocus, ref.focus(), focus trap or role=dialog anywhere around these sites (grep for .focus(/autoFocus/aria-modal finds only unrelated text fields). The same happens on cancel. The stated consequence is wrong for this app's WebView2/Chromium engine, though. Chromium keeps a sequential-focus-navigation starting point where the removed element was, so the next Tab does not restart at the top of the document. It goes on from the old Delete position and normally lands on the question's own 'Confirm deletion' button, which comes first in ConfirmDelete.tsx:62. Escape still cancels because the listener sits on window. The impact is a lost screen-reader context, not a lost place in the Tab order.

The doc comment at lines 11-13 says it deliberately does not focus its confirm button, and it focuses nothing else either. title: Sliders write every intermediate value; dragging the buffer slider discards footage
claim: The buffer-length slider in Recording.tsx:393-409 uses `onChange={(seconds) => patchConfig({ buffer: { ...config.buffer, seconds, ... } })}` and the memory-budget slider at Recording.tsx:468-477 does the same, so every intermediate drag value is written. scenario: The buffer holds 10 minutes; the user drags the length slider down past 30 s and back to 5 min. The ring was trimmed to 30 s mid-drag and the footage is gone; the memory slider drops old GOPs the same way. Each tick is a synchronous `set_config` on the Tauri main thread running `replace_config`, which writes the config file (`config::save`), may spawn an audio-refresh thread enumerating the process tree, and calls `apply_autostart` (registry read), `overlay::reposition` and `console::relayout` - 30-100 times per drag. title: No ESLint config although eslint-disable comments exist; floating promises go undetected

Small real nits: a non-string rejection becomes the generic "Something went wrong.", and an error arriving after SignedIn unmounts (sign-out while a request is in flight) is silently dropped.
votes.reachable_by: Nobody at runtime, since it is a code-structure observation. The error path itself runs when a friends_accept/remove/block invoke rejects.
votes.fix_assessment: There is no store-level notify function to route into; one would have to be built. It could not live in useFriends, which is replaced on every backend push. Lifting `error` state into SignedIn and passing a setter down, or using a small React context, would do the job more simply.

title: Outdated comment in store.ts about saving on every keystroke
claim: The comment at store.ts:490 about saving on every keystroke is outdated; `ClipMeta` now saves on blur.
scenario: Misleading comment for maintainers.
fix: Update or remove the comment.

votes.evidence: src/store.ts:489-491 `async updateClip(id, meta) { // Apply locally first: typing happens in a field that should show every keystroke right away, saving runs alongside.` Neither caller feeds keystrokes into the store. ClipMeta.tsx Field keeps its own `draft` state (265) and calls onSave from a 500 ms debounce (`window.setTimeout(() => commitRef.current(), 500)`, 296-300), on blur (`onBlur={commit}`, 320/330) and on unmount (304). Clips.tsx NameField also keeps a local draft and calls updateClip only from `commit` on blur/Enter (727-735, 764).
votes.corrected_claim: The comment is stale: no caller passes every keystroke to updateClip, because both fields keep their own draft. But ClipMeta does not save only on blur. It saves 500 ms after the last keystroke, on blur and on unmount; only the gallery's NameField saves on blur alone.
votes.reachable_by: Maintainers only; no runtime effect.
votes.fix_assessment: Rewording the comment is enough, e.g. 'apply locally first so the gallery and the open viewer show the new value before the core answers'. Keep the optimistic update itself.

title: Meter keeps a 60 ms interval forever and animates width
claim: `Meter` (Controls.tsx:163-197) keeps a 60 ms `setInterval` per meter for its whole lifetime and animates `width`, which triggers layout.
scenario: Each visible meter runs a timer and forces layout continuously, even when levels are idle.
fix: Use a ref plus `transform: scaleX` driven by requestAnimationFrame.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/Controls.tsx:170-176 `const timer = setInterval(() => setShown((current) => (current < 0.005 ? 0 : current * 0.78)), 60); return () => clearInterval(timer); }, []);` runs for the whole mount. Controls.tsx:186 `transition-[width] duration-75 ease-linear` with 188 `width: `${pct}%``. When idle the updater returns 0 for current state 0, and React bails out before scheduling a render: node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:9151-9161 `eagerState = alternate(currentState, action); ... if (objectIs(eagerState, currentState)) return (enqueueUpdate$1(fiber, queue, update, 0), ...` with no scheduleUpdateOnFiber. pct is also clamped to 0 below -60 dB (181), so the style string does not change. Only usage: src/routes/AudioMixer.tsx:603-605 SourceMeter.
votes.corrected_claim: Each Meter does keep a 60 ms interval for its lifetime and animates `width`. But it does not force layout while idle: once `shown` reaches 0, setShown(c => 0) is eagerly bailed out by React (no render, no DOM write, no layout). The idle cost is one cheap timer tick per meter every 60 ms. Layout work only happens while a source carries signal (level > ~0.001), when the bar has to move anyway, and it is limited to one small bar per mixer source.
votes.reachable_by: Audio mixer page with sources: timers tick per meter always; layout happens only while levels are non-zero.
votes.fix_assessment: A ref plus transform: scaleX (with transform-origin left) and rAF would avoid layout and the idle timer. Clearing the interval when shown hits 0 and restarting it on a rising level is a smaller change. The gain is marginal either way.

title: Tray icon sent as a 64 KB JSON number array
claim: accent.ts:142 sends the 64 KB tray icon to the core as a JSON number array (`Array.from(pixels)`).
scenario: Every accent refresh (every 80 ms in RGB mode) serializes and parses a large JSON array over IPC.
fix: Send the pixels as binary.

votes.evidence: src/lib/accent.ts:67 `const ICON_SIZE = 128;` (128*128*4 = 65,536 bytes) and 142 `.then((pixels) => api.setLogoIcon(Array.from(pixels), ICON_SIZE))`, with src/lib/ipc.ts:46 `setLogoIcon: (rgba: number[], size: number) => invoke<void>("set_logo_icon", { rgba, size })` sending a JSON number array, deserialized as `rgba: Vec<u8>` at src-tauri/src/commands.rs:805. But this happens only inside `take()` (132-145), debounced by ICON_MS=250 (139-144), with the comment 'not on every turn of the RGB hue, only when the accent itself changes'. The 80 ms refresh (146-148, 157) only calls applyAccent, which writes CSS variables. take() runs on getConfig at start-up and on 'accent-changed', which the core emits only when `previous.accent() != next.accent()` (commands.rs:91-95).
votes.corrected_claim: The tray icon is sent as an about 64K-element JSON number array (about 200 KB of JSON). It is sent once at start-up and once per actual accent change, debounced 250 ms, not every 80 ms in RGB mode. In RGB mode the icon is drawn once with the full rainbow wheel and the 80 ms tick touches only CSS variables.
votes.reachable_by: A user changing the accent colour or mode in settings, at most once per 250 ms of picker movement.
votes.fix_assessment: Sending the Uint8ClampedArray as a raw body (Tauri 2 InvokeBody::Raw with size in a header, read via tauri::ipc::Request) would avoid the JSON blow-up. That works, but the payoff is negligible at this frequency.

title: Keyboard reorder in the mixer loses focus after one step
claim: `nudge` with ArrowDown (AudioMixer.tsx:201-208) makes React move the focused row's DOM node, so focus is lost after one step.
scenario: A keyboard user presses ArrowDown on a source's grip to move it; after one move focus is lost and further presses do nothing.
fix: Re-focus the grip after the move.

votes.evidence: src/routes/AudioMixer.tsx:201-207 `const nudge = (id, delta) => { ... [sources[from], sources[to]] = [sources[to], sources[from]]; patchConfig({ sources }); }`; src/store.ts:362-364 `async patchConfig(patch) { const config = { ...get().config, ...patch }; set({ config });` (optimistic, synchronous re-render); AudioMixer.tsx:254-256 rows are `config.sources.map((source) => <Card key={source.id} ...>` and the grip is a child `<span role="button" tabIndex={0} ... onKeyDown={... nudge(source.id, delta)}>` (AudioMixer.tsx:298-319). Nothing in the file calls focus() (grep 'focus' only hits class names at :322/:339). React is 19.2.8 (node_modules/react-dom/package.json) and react-dom-client contains no `moveBefore`, so keyed reorders use insertBefore/appendChild. For a swap [A,B,..] -> [B,A,..] React's reconcileChildrenArray keeps B (oldIndex 1 >= lastPlacedIndex) and re-places A (oldIndex 0 < lastPlacedIndex). ArrowDown on A therefore detaches and re-inserts the focused row's DOM node; Chromium/WebView2 resets document.activeElement to body when the focused subtree is removed, so the next ArrowDown goes to <body> and nudge is never called. ArrowUp on B leaves B's node in place, so focus survives, which matches the finding's ArrowDown-only scenario. useFlip (src/lib/useFlip.ts) only animates transforms and does not restore focus.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use by the local user: a keyboard user who Tabs to a source's grip in the Audio mixer (shown when there are 2+ sources) and presses ArrowDown. It happens every time in the WebView2 (Chromium) runtime. ArrowUp is not affected. Workarounds exist: Tab back to the grip, or press ArrowUp on the row below to make the same swap with focus kept.
votes.fix_assessment: Correct and small. After patchConfig, re-focus the moved row's grip, for example with a ref map keyed by source.id plus a useLayoutEffect or requestAnimationFrame that focuses `[aria-label="Move <label>"]` in the row with data-flip=id. Announcing the new position through an aria-live region would also help screen-reader users.

votes.evidence: src/routes/AudioMixer.tsx:201-207 nudge swaps two entries and calls patchConfig, which sets config synchronously (src/store.ts:362-364 `set({ config })`). Rows are keyed `key={source.id}` (AudioMixer.tsx:256), so React keeps the same Card/grip DOM nodes and moves one with insertBefore. For a one-step swap React's lastPlacedIndex logic moves the row whose old index is lower, so on ArrowDown the focused row is the one moved and the claim's mechanism is right that far. But react-dom 19.2.8 saves and restores focus around every commit: node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:13791 `root = getActiveElementDeep(root)` -> `selectionInformation = { focusedElem: root, ... }` (13857) before mutation, and after commitMutationEffects (17980-17993): `if (curFocusedElem !== priorFocusedElem && priorFocusedElem && ... containsNode(priorFocusedElem.ownerDocument.documentElement, priorFocusedElem))` ... `priorFocusedElem.focus()` (18066-18067). The grip span is still in the document after the move, so React focuses it again in the same commit. useFlip (src/lib/useFlip.ts) only runs Web Animations transforms and does not touch focus; Card (src/components/ui/Card.tsx:8-21) is a plain div.
votes.reachable_by: Keyboard user pressing ArrowUp/ArrowDown on a mixer row's grip; React restores focus, so the claimed loss does not occur.
votes.fix_assessment: Not needed: React already re-focuses the moved element after the commit. An explicit re-focus would do nothing (at most it could guard against a future change that remounts the row).

title: Clip gallery is unvirtualized and unmemoized; each tile pays for an uncached toLocaleDateString
claim: format.ts:24 does `new Date(ts).toLocaleDateString("en-US", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` once per tile per render (Clips.tsx:625); measured in Node/V8 at 63-81 ms per 1000 calls versus about 1 ms with a cached `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. `visible` (Clips.tsx:199-225) and every tile are rebuilt inline on every render (each search keystroke, `clips-changed`, `links` change, rename or confirm-state change). Each tile carries 2-4 `Pill`s with `backdrop-blur-md` (Card.tsx:38) plus heart/action buttons with `backdrop-blur-md` (Clips.tsx:557, :1180), so hundreds of backdrop-filter surfaces re-blur while scrolling. On first visit every tile, including off-screen ones, gets `cb-tile-in`.
scenario: With a large library (hundreds to 1000 clips), every keystroke in search or any clips-changed event re-renders all tiles and reformats every date, and scrolling re-blurs hundreds of surfaces, making the gallery sluggish.
fix: Hoist `const DATE = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(...)` in format.ts; extract a `ClipTile` wrapped in `React.memo` with stable id-keyed callbacks and memoize `visible` with `useMemo([clips, query, filter])`; add `content-visibility:auto; contain-intrinsic-size:auto 300px` to tiles or virtualize rows (e.g. `@tanstack/react-virtual`), so `useFlip` animates only mounted rows; replace `backdrop-blur` on tile chrome with solid `bg-black/60`; pass `updateClip` into `NameField` instead of subscribing per tile.

title: Mixer source label saves on every keystroke; a stale reply can drop typed characters
claim: AudioMixer.tsx:333-337 has `onChange={(e) => upsertSource({ ...source, label: e.target.value })}`, and store.ts:418-423 then does `set({ config: await api.updateAudioSource(source) })` unconditionally (last reply wins, no version guard). The same last-reply-wins problem affects gain, mute and solo.
scenario: Each keystroke means one IPC call, `replace_config`, a config file write and an audio-refresh thread. If a reply arrives after the next keystroke (main thread busy with a file dialog or slow disk), the store snaps the label back to the older value; the controlled input jumps and the next keystroke is appended to the stale text, losing characters. (Character loss under load is likely.)
fix: Keep a draft label and commit on blur/Enter, as `NameField` already does (Clips.tsx:697-771). Add the version guard from FC-1 to `upsertSource`/`removeSource`.

title: Mock data is the real store's initial config and its fallback in Tauri mode
claim: store.ts:164 initialises the store with `config: mock.mockConfig`, and store.ts:263 loads with `load("Reading the settings", api.getConfig, get().config)`, i.e. the mock config is the fallback if `get_config` fails, also in Tauri mode.
scenario: Until `getConfig` returns, the Dashboard shows fake values ("3 audio sources", "1080p60 · NVENC"). If `get_config` fails, the app marks itself `ready` with the mock config; the next `patchConfig` writes fake PIDs as audio sources, clipDir `C:\Users\user\Videos\ClippiBoy`, the mock hotkeys and `token: "mock-token"` into the user's real config. The core keeps a token only if it arrives empty, so the Stream Deck stops working. (Code path confirmed; failure unlikely but damaging.)
fix: Use `config: AppConfig | null` (or a `loaded` flag), don't render config-dependent routes until loaded, never fall back to mock in Tauri, and make `patchConfig` refuse to run before load.

also.title: UI starts from the mock config and `set_config` saves whatever whole config it is sent
also.claim: store.ts:164 has `config: mock.mockConfig`, and the main UI is not gated on `ready`. `patchConfig` (store.ts:362-368) sends `{...get().config, ...patch}`. `set_config` (commands.rs:54-68) keeps the real token only when the incoming one is empty. The mock has `token: "mock-token"` and `clipDir: "C:\\Users\\user\\…"` (mock.ts:86, :121).
also.fix: Start the UI config as `null` and gate the UI on it. Better, make `set_config` accept a typed patch, or reject a config that does not match the current revision. Never accept `control.token` from the UI.

title: Errors only show at the bottom of Settings and are never cleared
claim: Every failing store action calls `set({ lastError })` (`updateClip`, `setFavorite`, `setClipTags`, `patchConfig`, `clearGame`, `toggleBuffer`, `refreshTargets` and others), but `lastError` is only displayed in settings/index.tsx:80-84, and nothing ever sets `lastError: null` after the initial state (store.ts:188).
scenario: A failed rename or heart in the gallery gives no feedback at all. A startup error such as "Reading applications failed" sits under every Settings tab forever.
fix: Add a store-level `notify(kind, msg)` that feeds `Toasts` (which should also get `role="status"`/`aria-live`). Make `lastError` dismissible, or drop it.

also.title: Screenshot save errors are silent
also.claim: When saving a screenshot edit fails, the UI only resets the Save button. The error goes into `lastError` (store.ts:598-609), which is displayed solely on the Settings page (settings/index.tsx:80-84); nothing is emitted as a notice. This is despite the comment at ShotViewer.tsx:640 implying the error is surfaced.
also.fix: In `write_screenshot`, call `crate::notify(&app, "error", …)` on `Err`. Alternatively add a client-side toast to `Toasts.tsx`.

title: Clearing a game makes one IPC write per clip and change events undo the optimistic update mid-loop
claim: `clearGame` in store.ts:570-578 loops `await api.updateClip(...)` then `await get().fileClip(...)` per clip. Each `update_clip` runs `announce_change`, which emits `clips-changed` (commands.rs:941), and the listener at store.ts:302-310 re-reads the full clip list each time.
scenario: Removing a game with 200 clips means 200 writes, 200 full-list IPC reads and gallery re-renders. The re-reads restore the game on clips not yet processed, so the chip comes back and counts down. A failure partway through leaves the UI out of sync with no rollback.
fix: Add a single `clear_game(game)` core command that runs in one transaction and announces once.

title: EngineStatus fields are dropped by the store and never shown
claim: The `EngineStatus` fields `droppedFrames`, `fps`, `freeBytes`, `gameSeconds` and `encoder` are dropped by store.ts:273-285 and never shown in the UI.
scenario: Health data the core already sends (dropped frames, real encoder, free disk space, game session) is invisible to the user.
fix: Keep these fields in the store and surface them (e.g. a health panel).

votes.evidence: The store does pick only some fields: src/store.ts:273-285 sets bufferActive, recording, recordingSeconds, recordingBytes, bufferedSeconds, screenFallback, bufferBytes, rateControl, detectedGame, and leaves out droppedFrames/encoder/fps/gameSeconds/freeBytes. But the in-game console window (src-tauri/src/console.rs:59 `WebviewUrl::App("console.html")`) listens to the same event and shows all five. src/console/Console.tsx:349 `listen<EngineStatus>("engine-status", (e) => { setStatus(e.payload);`. Line 831 `<Stat label="FPS" value={status.fps.toFixed(0)} .../>`. Lines 840-842 show `${status.droppedFrames} total`. Line 849 `value={(status.encoder ?? "—").toUpperCase()}`. Lines 576-578 build `sessionTime(status.gameSeconds)` and `${formatSize(status.freeBytes)} free`, rendered at 1047-1049. Trend.tsx:57-66 also uses fps and droppedFrames.
votes.corrected_claim: Only the main window's zustand store leaves these fields out, and the main window does not show them. The console overlay, which is part of the same UI, displays FPS, dropped frames, the encoder, game session time and free disk space live, so the data is not invisible to the user.
votes.reachable_by: Not a defect. At most a product choice about whether the main window should also show health stats.
votes.fix_assessment: No fix is needed. Showing the stats in the main window too would be a feature request, not a bug fix.
